decisions.design: Agreed with the Guardian before building (answers A to D). A new append-only event table instead of reusing offline revocation, which cannot be undone and hides the request from its owner. Withdrawn now is the newest event by sequence number; offline revocation stays separate and stronger, so a revoked request can be neither withdrawn nor restored.
decisions.authority: Only the owning principal (same subject and issuer). Anyone else, and an unknown request, get the same refusal. One command id per decision: a repeat answers with how things stand now; the same id for another decision or request is refused the same way (a concurrent reuse is mapped to the same 42501).
decisions.when: Any time until the team has closed or cancelled the mission (CLOSED or CANCELLED answer not-withdrawable). Withdrawing deletes nothing, so after delivery it is allowed and delivered reports stay readable to the owner. Withdrawing needs the control open; restoring never does, so a paused control can never trap a withdrawal.
decisions.team: No customer function writes the team's mission. The team sees nothing in this PR, and the dialog promises nothing about what the team sees; S4's follow-up shows 'Withdrawn by the customer on <date>' read only. The owner should not open the control until that is merged.
decisions.reason: 10 to 500 characters of the person's own words. Stored only in the private event table, returned only to its owner, never in the domain event payload, the audit trail or an error. Whether the team may read it later is an owner privacy decision; exposing it is one function change. The dialog says: '10 to 500 characters. Only you can see this reason.' The length is counted in characters (code points) in the form, the schema and the database.
decisions.outbound: A withdrawn request sends no mission mail and no Pulse message. A message is blocked if the request was withdrawn at any time since the message (or the Move) was made, or is now, or is muted; the Move enqueue checks after both advisory locks; the claim checks again with the message's own creation time. Restoring never sends or queues anything, and a mute and a withdrawal together answer withdrawn.
decisions.installOrder: Optional installs need an explicit install action (AGENTS.md). The withdrawal module is therefore never part of a base run: apply=yes with every action unchanged installs nothing of it. It is installed, control closed, only as the first step of an explicit mission mail or notifications install (real-use schema, then withdrawal, then 0003 or 0005). The withdrawal migrator never applies the real-use schema itself: when that schema is not current it stops with a plain message and writes nothing. Opening withdrawal is refused (configureRequestWithdrawal) while an installed mission mail or notifications module lacks 0003 or 0005, so the promise to stop emailing cannot be opened ahead of the mail guards; pausing is never refused. Opening is a separate owner decision, after the staff signal is merged.
decisions.undo: Ten seconds of Undo after withdrawing, then Restore Request on the Withdrawn filter at any time while the request is not revoked.
decisions.process: The database module and its tests were written together and shown to fail with the migration directory removed; the Move and mail effects were tested after the guards; the lock of the in-flight dialog was proven by removing it, which failed its test. The browser spec was written after the component.

notRun: The saved requests list with the real service and the module installed in a browser: the verification seed has none of the modules on, so the list is covered through the fixture and the real database tests.
Applying the migrations anywhere, or opening the control. The owner does that, after the staff signal is merged.

The install workflow: .github/workflows/install-customer-modules.yml already has 25 inputs, the limit, so withdrawal is not wired to it. An explicit mission_mail_action or notifications_action install brings it in with its control closed; enabling is a script operation (REQUEST_WITHDRAWAL_ACTION) until a later change consolidates the reason inputs.
sensitive: Yes. This changes what a customer can do to a request the team may already be working on, what the team can see, and what is sent. The owner reviews and merges.

guardianFixes.installer: Removed from the base run; prerequisite of explicit mail installs only; migrator never applies real-use; refuse to open before mail upgrades (Codex P1).
guardianFixes.moves: A Move the team set on a withdrawn request is left out of Your Move with the request, and returns when it is restored.
guardianFixes.copy: The dialog no longer says what the Corridra team sees.
guardianFixes.closed: Withdraw Request is hidden for CLOSED and CANCELLED requests (the database check stays).
guardianFixes.counts: The Withdrawn count is every withdrawal the person has; a note says more may be on later pages while there are more pages.
guardianFixes.length: The reason is counted in characters in the form (the schema and database already were); the textarea no longer cuts at 500 UTF-16 units.
guardianFixes.outbox: Withdraw and restore events go to the domain and audit trail but not the outbox, matching the mute precedent.
guardianFixes.replay: Reusing a command id for another decision is refused with 42501 and answered 403, by design; there is no version: the newest event wins and only the owner toggles.
guardianFixes.body: The route's body bound is 4000 bytes (was 2000): 500 four-byte characters plus the JSON envelope is about 2.1 KB, and 500 characters JSON escapes to six bytes each is about 3.2 KB, so a valid reason was refused with 413 (Codex P2). The oversized-body test now sends 5000 bytes.
